outcome: Give government cio / agency operations director a governed method to improve cost per completed collection route using bin fill sensors, truck capacity and service addresses, with final decisions…
overview: Municipal Waste Route Optimisation addresses resource allocation is planned in silos, producing avoidable delays and occasionally infeasible instructions in government and public sector operations. The first proof of value uses bin fill sensors, truck capacity and service addresses. It produces a reviewed operational recommendation and a traceable decision record. The commercial success measure is cost per completed collection route, established from customer baseline data before any improvement is claimed.

benefits.limits: Basis: design hypothesis. Depends on source quality and named decision owner

benefits.limits: Basis: customer-specific hypothesis. No uplift promised; validate in controlled pilot

scope:
Delivery model: Redington or approved implementation partner, eligibility and staffing pending confirmation.
Duration: Discovery and design first; pilot and rollout durations depend on data access and scope; no fixed commitment.
1) Discover source quality and baseline: bin fill sensors, truck capacity and service addresses; define cost per completed collection route and data-processing boundary.
2) Design control points, security and connector contracts; obtain owner approval from Government CIO / Agency Operations Director.
3) Implement one bounded workflow, instrument missing-data exceptions and system-of-record write-back.
4) Test positive, negative, privilege, partial-data and rollback cases including replay disruption and edge cases with hard constraints enforced.
5) Review KPI in the pilot, document evidence, perform training and agree transition.
deliverables: Agreed test threshold for cost per completed collection route
